W2 variable labels read '<stem> - <behaviour>'; the stem 'In the past week, to reduce your risk of being infected by or passing on the coronavirus to others, on how many days of the week have you:' went to instructions and the behaviour to item_text (label line breaks collapsed to single spaces; nothing else changed), 16/16 identical to the W2 Q86 grid rows and to the measures docx 2.2.7.15 list. W3 (Phase 1 recontacts only, Q418) administered only items 1-7, with a shorter stem 'In the past week, on how many days have you:' and slightly reworded behaviours (e.g. item 2 'Exercised outside the house once a day' vs W2 'Exercised outside once a day (either alone or with members of your household)?'; item 4 'Met up with friends or extended family outside home'; item 5 '...more than 2 people in a park or public space'); items 8-16 are W2 only. The build pools items 1-7 across W2 and W3 under one code, so the shipped text is the W2 wording throughout (the fuller administration, 16 items) in a single section, and the W3 variant is disclosed in public_note. This follows the batch_715 hygiene precedent (ship the earlier wave's wording for pooled items, disclose the other). option_text = .sav value labels 1=Not at all, 2=1-2 days a week, 3=3-4 days a week, 4=Most days, 5=Every day, identical across all 23 variables in both waves and matching both questionnaire grid headers. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per wave x item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 115/115 (W2 16x5 + W3 7x5); live 30658 rows, 1622 ids, W2 1406 per item, W3 1166 per item (items 1-7). Data caveat (notes only): item 11 'Reminded your children about hygienic practices or social distancing rules?' was shown to all W2 respondents with no skip; 734 of 1406 reported 0 children in household or living alone (W2_Children_household in {0,-9}), and 205 of those answered above 'Not at all' (30/15/41/119 at resp 2-5) -- possibly children living elsewhere, so not asserted as an error. Rights: study-authored items (C19PRC-UK), no third-party instrument; deposit CC BY 4.0. English administration. Dictionary Description 'Weekly lockdown risk behaviours (16 items)' matches the live data (Step 3b OK); instrument field uses the measures docx's section title.
